title: U.S. House · North Dakota At-Large

context.text: Incumbent Julie Fedorchak (R) defeated Alex Balazs 72.8%-27.0% in the June 9, 2026 Republican primary. Trygve Hammer won the Democratic primary essentially unopposed with 99.8% of the vote after Vern Thompson withdrew.

summary.text: Julie Fedorchak is the Republican incumbent for North Dakota's at-large House seat. She worked in communications, state government, and her own communications business before serving on the North Dakota Public Service Commission from 2013 to 2025, and was elected to Congress in 2024. She serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, and her official issues pages focus on energy, agriculture, and the budget.

background.text: Born in Williston, North Dakota, and raised in Fargo; the youngest of eight children, she graduated from Bismarck Century High School and describes herself as a fourth-generation North Dakotan.
Earned a B.A. in journalism from the University of North Dakota in 1991; began her career as a communications and media relations specialist.
Served as a spokesperson for Gov. Ed Schafer (R) from 1995 to 2000; her official biography describes the role as communications director.
Founded a communications business that she says she ran for 10 years, working with clients in business, government, and politics and authoring several books and articles.
Became North Dakota state director for U.S. Sen. John Hoeven (R) in 2011.
Appointed to the North Dakota Public Service Commission in November 2012 by Gov. Jack Dalrymple, sworn in January 2, 2013, and served until 2025.

Served as president of the National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners (NARUC), a post her official biography says ended in November 2024, and as president of the Organization of MISO States (OMS).
Won the 2024 general election for North Dakota's at-large House seat with 69.2% of the vote over Trygve Hammer, succeeding Kelly Armstrong, and took office January 3, 2025.
Serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, including its Communications and Technology, Energy, and Environment subcommittees, for the 2025-2026 Congress.
Won the June 9, 2026 Republican primary with 72.8% of the vote over Alex Balazs.
According to her official biography, she lives in Mandan with her husband, Mike, and serves on the Board of Trustees of the University of Mary.

priorities.text: Says she is focused on energy affordability, reliability, sustainability and security, and wants to expand domestic energy production and lower costs.
Says she supports balancing the federal budget and rooting out wasteful spending, citing the scale of the national debt.
Says agriculture is the backbone of North Dakota's economy and supports improving the Farm Bill, strengthening crop insurance, and reducing regulations on farmers and ranchers.

positions.summary: As a member of the Energy and Commerce Committee, says she is working to expand domestic energy production, including fossil fuels, rather than restrict it, and frames energy policy around affordability and reliability.
Frames federal deficits as a spending problem and calls for balancing the budget and cutting waste rather than raising taxes.

record.text: Sits on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, including the Communications and Technology, Energy, and Environment subcommittees, in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Trygve Hammer
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 9, 2026 Democratic primary with 99.8% of the vote after Vern Thompson withdrew; previously the Democratic nominee for this seat in 2024.

summary.text: Trygve Hammer is the Democratic nominee for North Dakota's at-large House seat. A U.S. Naval Academy graduate and Marine Corps veteran who grew up in Velva, he worked as an airline pilot, defense contractor, and security consultant and now writes a newsletter. He ran unsuccessfully for the Public Service Commission in 2022 and for this seat in 2024, and says he is running to restore Congress's constitutional powers over war, tariffs, and spending.

background.text: Says he grew up in Velva, North Dakota, and graduated from Velva High School.
Says he enlisted in the Navy as a nuclear power machinist's mate before earning an appointment to the U.S. Naval Academy, from which he received a bachelor's degree in 1990.

Served in the U.S. Marine Corps and Marine Corps Reserve until 2010, including as a helicopter pilot, forward air controller, military attaché at the U.S. Embassy in Rome, and instructor; says he flew CH-53D helicopters and led an infantry unit in Iraq in 2003.
Worked as an airline pilot, defense contractor and security consultant, and later as a writer and teacher; says he writes a newsletter called Punching Up.

Ran unsuccessfully as a Democrat for North Dakota House District 6 in 2020, finishing third in a two-seat race, and for the North Dakota Public Service Commission in 2022, receiving 29.5% against Republican incumbent Sheri Haugen-Hoffart.
Was the Democratic nominee for the at-large U.S. House seat in 2024, losing to Julie Fedorchak with 30.4% of the vote; won the 2026 Democratic primary with 99.8% of the vote.

priorities.text: During his 2024 campaign for this seat, his website listed lowering prescription drug prices, protecting Social Security benefits, and support for rural schools and communities among his priorities.

positions.summary: His 2024 campaign website said the government should not intrude on personal medical decisions and called for protecting women's freedom to make their own healthcare decisions.
His 2024 campaign website said profitable corporations and the ultra-wealthy need to pay their fair share of taxes.

candidates.researchNotes: Hammer has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and no 2026 campaign website content was located; priorities and positions above are drawn from his 2024 campaign website, as quoted by Ballotpedia, and may not reflect any changes for 2026.

candidates.name: Helene Neville

summary.text: Helene Neville is an independent candidate for North Dakota's at-large House seat. A nurse with more than 42 years of experience, she describes herself in her Ballotpedia survey as a public health professional, cancer survivor, author, entrepreneur, and endurance athlete, and says she is running on health care, the economy, disparities, and term and age limits.

background.text: Earned a high school diploma from Burlington High School and an associate degree from Iowa Western Community College in 1984.
Works as a nurse; says she has cared for patients for more than 42 years in hospitals, clinics, rural communities, tribal health systems, correctional facilities, and public health programs.
Says she was diagnosed with Stage IV lymphoma in 2020 and survived, and that she has run more than 16,600 miles across the United States, Canada, Mexico, and Puerto Rico, including fundraising runs.
Says she is limiting campaign fundraising to $30,000, will not accept PAC contributions, and is traveling to every incorporated community in North Dakota.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, Candidate Connection survey response, or other public statements found for Helene Neville in the time available.

candidates.name: Charles Tuttle

summary.text: Charles Tuttle is an independent candidate for North Dakota's at-large House seat. He has run for statewide and federal office several times since 2018, and ran in the June 2026 special primary for state Superintendent of Public Instruction.

background.text: Ran as an independent for North Dakota's at-large U.S. House seat in 2018, receiving 4.1% of the vote in a race won by Kelly Armstrong.
Ran for North Dakota Superintendent of Public Instruction in 2020, finishing third in the nonpartisan primary with 19.7%, then as a write-in candidate in the general election.
Ran as an independent for North Dakota Secretary of State in 2022, receiving 9.2% of the vote in a race won by Michael Howe.
Lost the June 9, 2026 special nonpartisan primary for Superintendent of Public Instruction, receiving 14.4%.
